source: Microsoft Excel Math&Trigonometry + Statistical functions reference (support.microsoft.com), fetched 2026-07-11
note: 50 genuinely ambiguous functions classified by parallel agents against the live 718-cell library; the other 141 (all trig/hyperbolic/inverse-trig, all continuous probability distributions + special functions, arbitrary-arity aggregates, RAND family, PI) hand-prefiltered with high confidence per established host_only/out_of_scope reasoning from prior waves.

entries.name: ABS
entries.description: Returns the absolute value of a number
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: abs_i16
entries.repr: run(x: i16) -> u16
entries.reason: docs/cell-index.md:779 lists `abs_i16` — "Absolute value of a signed 16-bit value, returned as u16 (correctly handles i16::MIN, whose magnitude 32768 doesn't fit back in i16)." This is exactly Excel's ABS(number): single input, returns the magnitude, and it already handles the one edge case (i16::MIN / most-negative value) a naive implementation would get wrong. Excel's ABS is single-arity (one number in, one non-negative number out), not the arbitrary-arity family (contrast NPV's value1..value254 gap) — abs_i16's signature matches Excel's real contract directly, no array-state or composition needed. Distinguish from abs_diff_i16/abs_diff/abs_diff_u32 (two-input difference-of-two-values cells, a different function family — those would cover ABS(a-b), not bare ABS(x)) and from negate_i16 (returns -x, the complementary sign-flip op, cited in cell-index.md:792 as distinct from abs_i16 precisely because it doesn't take the magnitude).

entries.name: CEILING
entries.description: Rounds a number to the nearest integer or to the nearest multiple of significance
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: snap_up (bounds pack, u16) — with snap_up_u32 as the wide u32 sibling for larger magnitudes
entries.reason: Excel's CEILING(number, significance) rounds number UP, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance. `snap_up` (docs/cell-index.md:111, cell80/cells/bounds/snap_up.rs) is `run(x: u16, step: u16) -> u16` = "Round x UP to the nearest multiple of step" -- semantically identical for the domain cell80 can represent (non-negative integers, positive significance, which is the common/well-defined case for CEILING; Excel's real-number and mixed-sign edge cases fall outside u16 anyway). Verified the implementation matches Excel's own "already-a-multiple returns unchanged" rule: `snap_up(10, 5) = ((10-1)/5+1)*5 = 10` (unchanged), `snap_up(11, 5) = 15` (rounds up). `snap_up_u32` (line 112) extends this past u16's 65535 ceiling. One documented divergence: Excel's CEILING(n, 0) returns 0, while snap_up(x, 0) returns x unchanged -- but this is cell80's library-wide convention for the zero-step edge case (round_to_multiple and snap_down do the same), not something unique to this one function, so it doesn't block a covered verdict.

entries.name: CEILING.MATH
entries.description: Rounds a number up, to the nearest integer or to the nearest multiple of significance
entries.composable_author_reason: well-known-expected: CEILING.MATH is a canonical, widely-used Excel rounding primitive (paired with FLOOR.MATH) whose mode-argument negative-number convention is a well-documented fragile detail (easy to invert by hand, easy to confuse with plain CEILING/CEILING.PRECISE's differing negative-number behavior) -- the same "recognizability + convention fragility" reasoning already applied to PMT/FV/PV.
entries.reason:
Excel's real signature is CEILING.MATH(number, [significance], [mode]): round number up to the nearest multiple of significance, except for negative numbers where mode (0 default = toward zero, nonzero = away from zero) flips the direction; significance's sign is ignored (abs taken). The core "round up to nearest multiple of step" arithmetic is already covered for the unsigned/positive case by snap_up/snap_up_u32, and the "round down to nearest multiple" needed for the mode=0-negative case is covered by snap_down/snap_down_u32. So the whole function is glue: decompose number into (sign, magnitude), pick snap_up_u32 (number>=0, or number<0 with mode!=0, i.e. away-from-zero) vs snap_down_u32 (number<0 with mode==0, i.e. toward-zero) on the magnitude, then re-apply the sign. That's caller-side composition of two existing cells' outputs, which by default would be composable-skip -- but it clears composable-author under reason 1 (well-known/expected functionality with convention fragility): CEILING.MATH is one of Excel's best-known rounding primitives, and its mode-flag negative-number direction is a textbook easy-to-get-backwards convention (frequently confused with plain CEILING's and CEILING.PRECISE's own different negative-number rules), exactly the kind of fragile, worth-encoding-once rule the amendment calls out (same shape as the PMT precedent).</reason>
<parameter name="cell80_id_or_composition">Composes from snap_up_u32 (SnapUpWide: round a u32 value UP to the nearest multiple of step) and snap_down_u32 (SnapDownWide: round a u32 value DOWN to the nearest multiple of step) -- both cited from docs/cell-index.md. Caller/glue: split number into (is_neg, magnitude); if !is_neg, result = snap_up_u32(magnitude, sig); if is_neg and mode==0, result = -snap_down_u32(magnitude, sig) (toward zero); if is_neg and mode!=0, result = -snap_up_u32(magnitude, sig) (away from zero); sig = abs(significance) computed by the caller (significance==0 short-circuits to 0, matching Excel).

entries.name: CEILING.PRECISE
entries.description: Rounds a number up regardless of sign, to the nearest integer or multiple of significance
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: Composes from snap_up / snap_up_u32 (rounds x UP to nearest multiple of step) for the non-negative branch, and snap_down / snap_down_u32 negated for the negative branch: ceiling_precise(x, s) = x>=0 ? snap_up(x, s) : -snap_down(-x, s), with the caller taking abs(s) before either call (Excel's own rule: CEILING.PRECISE ignores significance's sign entirely, always rounding toward +infinity -- unlike plain CEILING). Both existing cells already live in the checked-arithmetic pack (docs/cell-index.md lines ~107-112).
entries.repr: checked-int (u16/u32 domain, matching snap_up/snap_up_u32/snap_down/snap_down_u32's existing tier) -- no fractional/float representation needed since Excel's significance argument in practice is used at integer/grid granularity in this dialect's existing rounding-kernel family.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is CEILING.PRECISE(number, [significance]) -- fixed 2-arg (optional 2nd defaulting to 1), no array-state-field issue. The underlying operation is exactly the mathematical ceiling-to-multiple that snap_up/snap_up_u32 already compute for non-negative numbers; the only piece those unsigned cells don't cover is negative-number handling, and that reduces to snap_down on the absolute value, negated (a standard identity: ceil(x/s) = -floor(-x/s)). No new algorithm is needed, just sign-branch glue over two existing checked-arithmetic cells plus a caller-side abs/negate -- so it is technically composable, not a candidate. It clears reason 1 (well-known/expected): CEILING.PRECISE is a named, expected Excel Math&Trig function, and it is convention-fragile in exactly the way reason 1 calls out -- it silently ignores the sign of significance and always rounds toward +positive infinity, which is easy to conflate with plain CEILING's away-from-zero/sign-matched convention or with CEILING.MATH's mode-flag behavior (the same kind of sign/rounding-convention trap flagged for ISPMT in docs/excel-financial-map.md line 104). Authoring one canonical cell that encodes the branch+negate rule once (tested) is worth the retrieval tax; leaving it to be hand-re-derived at each call site risks silently reproducing plain-CEILING's away-from-zero bug for negative inputs.

entries.name: COMBIN
entries.description: Returns the number of combinations for a given number of objects
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: choose_u32
entries.reason: Excel COMBIN(number, number_chosen) returns C(n,k) = n!/(k!*(n-k)!), the count of k-element subsets of an n-element set, order not mattering, no repetition. This is exactly the binomial coefficient already shipped as choose_u32 (struct ChooseWide::run() -> u16), documented in docs/cell-index.md line 203 as the Binomial coefficient "n choose k" (nCr), checked, via the multiplicative running-division formula, escalates rather than silently wrapping. Signature and semantics match one-to-one: COMBIN takes exactly two required arguments, no array-state issue, no optional-argument ambiguity. Note: Excel's sibling COMBINA (combinations with repetition) is separately covered by choose_with_repetition (cell-index.md line 204), confirming the pack already distinguishes the two.

entries.name: COMBINA
entries.description: Returns the number of combinations with repetitions for a given number of items
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: choose_with_repetition (ChooseWithRepetition::run() -> u16)
entries.repr: u16 -> u32 internal (checked, escalates on overflow), same tier as choose_u32
entries.reason: Excel COMBINA(number, number_chosen) returns the multiset coefficient C(number+number_chosen-1, number_chosen) -- combinations with repetition. cell80's combinatorics pack already has exactly this: choose_with_repetition (ChooseWithRepetition::run(), docs/cell-index.md line 204), whose docstring is C(n+k-1, k) for "the number of ways to choose k items from n types when repeats are permitted" -- an exact 2-arg-to-2-arg match (n=number, k=number_chosen), not a fixed-arity narrowing of a variadic Excel signature (COMBINA takes exactly two scalar arguments in real Excel, no array-state gap here, unlike NPV/SUMPRODUCT-style functions).

entries.name: DECIMAL
entries.description: Converts a text representation of a number in a given base into a decimal number
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: None (closest analog: number_to_base, cell-index.md:521 -- opposite direction, base<=9 only, does not cover DECIMAL's real text/radix-36 signature)
entries.missing_capability: A string/text-typed argument (variable-length alphanumeric, digits 0-9 + letters A-Z) crossing the call boundary -- cell80's free-fn params and state fields are fixed-width u16/u32 numerics only; no text type exists in the dialect.
entries.reason: DECIMAL(text, radix) parses a variable-length alphanumeric string (digits 0-9 plus letters A-Z for radix 11-36) into its base-10 value. cell80's calling convention has no string/text parameter type at all -- confirmed directly in cell-index.md's own note on `excel_networkdays_intl` (id at cell-index.md:276), which deliberately diverges from Excel's weekend string/number argument encoding "since the dialect has no strings." The nearest existing cell, `number_to_base` (cell-index.md:521, `run(n: u16, base: u16) -> u16`), runs the *opposite* direction (decimal value -> base-b digit expansion re-displayed as a decimal literal) and is capped at `2 <= base <= 9` specifically because reassembling digits >9 as decimal-literal digits breaks down -- the same wall blocks a hand-rolled inverse: you cannot round-trip Excel's real radix-36 alphanumeric text through a u16/u32 numeric parameter, only a narrow radix<=9, digits-only pseudo-version, which is not DECIMAL's real signature (the same NPV-style misclassification the taxonomy doc's correction note warns against -- don't down-scope to what the encoding trick permits and call the real function covered/composable/candidate).

entries.name: EVEN
entries.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest even integer
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: Composes abs_i16 -> div_ceil_u32(mag, 2)*2 (trivial double, not a cell) -> negate_i16 (conditionally, if x < 0)
entries.reason: EVEN(number) = round number up, away from zero, to the nearest even integer (EVEN(3)=4, EVEN(2)=2, EVEN(-1)=-2, EVEN(0)=0). No existing cell80 id does this rounding operation -- is_even/is_even_u32 (cell-index.md lines 613-614) only test parity, they never round. But the operation itself is pure glue over cells that already exist, with zero iteration/convergence: mag = abs_i16(x) (signed-deltas, line 776) strips the sign; ceil_mag = div_ceil_u32(mag, 2) (checked-arithmetic, line 162) computes the ceiling quotient, and doubling it back (mag*2, a trivial shift, not its own cell) lands exactly on the next even integer at or above mag -- div_ceil_u32's own q+1-if-remainder technique (the same one frac_of_whole_ceil/percent_ceil already reuse) means an even input is returned unchanged and an odd input bumps by exactly 1 before the *2, so no separate parity-bump step is needed; result = negate_i16(ceil_mag) if x was negative else ceil_mag (signed-deltas, line 788) reapplies the original sign, and x=0 falls out correctly with no special case (abs_i16(0)=0, div_ceil_u32(0,2)=0). That's a 1-branch sign check gluing three existing cells' outputs, not a loop/case-analysis algorithm, so reason 2 (genuine complexity) doesn't apply and this isn't a misclassified candidate. Reason 1 (well-known/expected) does: EVEN is one of Excel's most familiar named rounding primitives, and its "away from zero" direction is genuinely easy to conflate with round-to-nearest (round_to_multiple's own ties-up convention, line 107) or with CEILING's toward-positive-infinity convention -- exactly the convention-fragility that already justified SYD/EFFECT/TBILLYIELD as composable-author in docs/excel-financial-map.md rather than composable-skip. A fractional (non-integer) "number" argument would route through the fixed-point pack's existing Q8.8 domain (int_to_q8_i16/q_to_int_i16, lines 328/345) the same way the compat layer already scales other real-valued Excel arguments (bps for PMT/FV rates) -- no missing dialect/harness capability (no array-state, no transcendental) is needed either way, so host_only does not apply.

entries.name: FACT
entries.description: Returns the factorial of a number
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: factorial_checked_u32 (cell80/cells/combinatorics/factorial_checked_u32.rs, entry FactorialChecked::run)
entries.repr: checked-int (u32)
entries.reason: Excel FACT(number) returns the factorial of a (truncated, non-negative) number, erroring #NUM! once it exceeds the representable range (171 and up). cell80's factorial_checked_u32 is exactly this operation: n! via a running checked product, escalating (halt 0xFF05, needs_wider_math) instead of silently wrapping once n! would exceed u32::MAX (n >= 13) — the same "escalate on overflow rather than misbehave" contract every checked-arithmetic cell in this library already carries, just with a narrower boundary (u32 vs. Excel's f64-backed 170! ceiling) than Excel's own. The taxonomy's `covered` bucket is about an existing cell already doing this operation, not a bit-exact range match (compare `day_count_act_365` covering YEARFRAC(...,3) despite its own fixed-width conventions), so this is covered rather than candidate. No other pack duplicates it: number-theory's `wilson_factorial_mod` is a distinct two-arg (k, m) mod-reduced building block underneath Wilson's theorem, not a plain factorial, and `double_factorial`/`permute_u32` are genuinely different sequences (n!! and nPr), not FACT.

entries.name: FACTDOUBLE
entries.description: Returns the double factorial of a number
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: double_factorial
entries.reason: Excel's FACTDOUBLE(number) returns n!! = n*(n-2)*(n-4)*...*(2 or 1). This is an exact match for the already-shipped `double_factorial` cell (combinatorics pack, docs/cell-index.md line 207): "The double factorial n!! = n*(n-2)*(n-4)*...*(2 or 1) (0!! = 1!! = 1 by convention), checked -- escalates instead of silently wrapping once n!! would exceed u32::MAX." Same operation, same 0!!/1!! convention, checked-overflow semantics compatible with Excel's #NUM! on out-of-range results. No new cell needed.

entries.name: FLOOR
entries.description: Rounds a number down, toward zero
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: snap_down (u16 domain, pack `bounds`); snap_down_u32 (wide u32 sibling, same pack)
entries.reason: Excel FLOOR(number, significance) rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance, staying on the near-zero side ("toward zero" per Excel's own line). That is exactly `snap_down`'s doc comment: "Round x DOWN to the nearest multiple of step (x if step == 0). Floor to grid" — `(x / step) * step` (integer truncating divide then multiply back), cell80/cells/bounds/snap_down.rs. `snap_down_u32` is the wide sibling for values beyond 65535. This mirrors the already-landed sibling classification for MROUND in cell80/data/math_server_catalog_map.json, which was marked `covered` -> `round_to_multiple` (the same pack's nearest-with-ties-up variant); FLOOR is round_to_multiple's round-down-only cousin, and CEILING is the corresponding snap_up. cell80's u16/u32 domain is unsigned-only, so Excel's "#NUM! if number and significance have mismatched signs" edge case never arises here (nothing to diverge on). The one real edge-case difference — Excel documents FLOOR(number, 0) as returning 0, while snap_down (like round_to_multiple) returns x unchanged when step==0 — is a pre-existing, already-accepted divergence in this exact library (round_to_multiple's doc comment states the identical "x if step == 0" convention and MROUND was still filed `covered` against it), so it doesn't change the classification here either.

entries.name: FLOOR.MATH
entries.description: Rounds a number down, to the nearest integer or to the nearest multiple of significance
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: div_floor_u32 + mul_checked_u32 (floor-to-multiple glue) plus new sign/mode case-analysis logic (no existing cell covers negative-number handling + the mode toggle)
entries.composable_author_reason: well-known-expected: Excel-named function with convention fragility -- default significance sign (matches number) and the mode argument's negative-number rounding-direction switch
entries.reason: Not covered: no existing cell floors a number to an arbitrary multiple of a significance. `div_floor_u32` (checked-arithmetic) only floors an unsigned integer division (a/b); `round_to_multiple`/`round_to_multiple_u32` round to the NEAREST multiple (ties up), which is a different operation from flooring. Base glue for the positive/unsigned case is straightforward composition: caller runs `div_floor_u32(number, significance)` then feeds that quotient into `mul_checked_u32(_, significance)` to get floor-to-multiple. But Excel's real signature is FLOOR.MATH(number, [significance], [mode]) over signed numbers, with (a) significance's default sign following number's sign when omitted, and (b) the mode argument switching rounding direction (toward zero vs away from zero) specifically for negative numbers -- neither of which any existing cell encodes, and this dialect has no i32 (per smag_add's own comment), so negative `number`/`significance` need the sign-magnitude case-analysis pattern smag_add/smag_div/mod_inverse already use. That sign-convention-plus-mode-switch is exactly the "easy to get subtly wrong re-deriving by hand" fragility the taxonomy amendment names under reason 1, and matches the precedent already set for ISPMT/EFFECT/TBILLYIELD in docs/excel-financial-map.md (composable-author, well-known + fragile convention/ordering), not the IRR/RATE misclassification trap (no iteration/convergence loop here, just finite case analysis, so it isn't secretly a `candidate`).

entries.name: FLOOR.PRECISE
entries.description: Rounds a number down regardless of sign, to the nearest integer or multiple of significance
entries.repr: f32 (softfloat/physics tier) -- new cell composing the already-implemented fdiv/ffloor/fmul kernels from rustz80/src/softfloat.rs's F32_KERNELS prelude (ffloor is round-toward-negative-infinity, exactly FLOOR.PRECISE's semantic) plus a sign-bit-clear for |significance| and a convention decision for omitted-vs-zero significance; no cell currently surfaces any of these kernels standalone.
entries.reason: Rounds a real number down toward -infinity to the nearest multiple of |significance| (sign of significance ignored, unlike plain FLOOR), significance optional (default 1). No existing cell covers this: snap_down/snap_down_u32 (cell-index.md:109-110) and div_floor_u32 (cell-index.md:164) only floor-to-multiple over the unsigned u16/u32 domain — no negative numbers, no fractional operands, no sign-agnostic significance, no omittable default (the same narrow-sibling trap flagged for NPV). It also isn't composable: the pieces it would need (fdiv, fmul, and critically ffloor — round-toward-negative-infinity on a real f32, documented in rustz80/src/softfloat.rs's F32_KERNELS rounding family) exist only as dialect-prelude kernel primitives DCE-inlined into whichever cell uses them, never exposed as a standalone cell (every f32-tier cell-index.md row — lerp_f32, kinetic_energy_f32, verlet_step_f32, norm2_f32, clamp_f32, matrix_solve_3x3, nth_root_f32 — is a composite named op, none a bare fdiv/ffloor/fmul cell). Composable requires gluing 1-2 EXISTING CELLS' outputs; kernels aren't cells and can't be chained across a call boundary, so there is nothing to compose from -- this needs one new cell authored, at the f32 tier (matching matrix_solve_3x3/kinetic_energy_f32/lerp_f32 precedent, since checked-int's unsigned domain can't do negative-floor and Q8.8's range is too narrow for general Excel magnitudes). New logic (not genuine algorithmic complexity -- no iteration/convergence, so this isn't a composable-author misclassification either): sign-agnostic |significance| via an f32 sign-bit clear (no new kernel needed), then ffloor(number/|significance|)*|significance| using the already-implemented fdiv/ffloor/fmul kernels, plus a domain decision for the omitted-vs-explicit-zero significance convention (Excel defaults to 1 when omitted but returns 0 for significance=0).

entries.name: GCD
entries.description: Returns the greatest common divisor
entries.missing_capability: Array-state fields: CellHost's runner zeros a state cell's fields before every run() and only round-trips named scalar fields, never arrays -- so Excel's arbitrary-length "value1, [value2], ..., [value255]" argument list cannot be represented as a single cell. Same gap documented for IRR/MIRR/NPV/FVSCHEDULE in docs/excel-financial-map.md.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is GCD(number1, [number2], ..., [number255]) -- arbitrary arity, same shape as NPV(rate, value1, [value2], ..., [value254]). cell80's number-theory pack already ships fixed small-arity siblings -- gcd (u16, 2-arg), gcd_u32 (wide, 2-arg), gcd3 (u16, 3-arg), gcd3_u32 (wide, 3-arg), all cited in docs/cell-index.md -- but per the exact NPV correction recorded in docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md and docs/excel-financial-map.md ("A FIXED small-arity sibling existing... does NOT make an arbitrary-arity Excel function covered"), a fixed-arity sibling cannot satisfy Excel's real variadic signature. The general case is blocked by the array-state-field gap (CellHost's runner zeros state every run(), never round-trips arrays across the call boundary), the same wall that put IRR/MIRR/NPV/FVSCHEDULE in host_only rather than covered/candidate. So GCD classifies host_only against its true signature, even though the practical 2- and 3-argument cases are already covered by gcd/gcd_u32/gcd3/gcd3_u32.

entries.name: INT
entries.description: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: q_to_int_i16
entries.repr: Q8.8 fixed-point (i16) -- the library's standard tier for representing non-integer "real" numbers (also used throughout money-bps, percent, fractions, statistics, excel-financial)
entries.reason: `q_to_int_i16` (cell80/cells/fixed-point, docs/cell-index.md line 344) already does exactly what Excel's INT does, in this dialect's terms: it decodes a signed Q8.8 fixed-point value back to a plain integer via an arithmetic (sign-propagating) right shift by 8, which the cell's own doc comment says "floors toward negative infinity for negatives" -- i.e. INT(-8.9)=-9 behavior, not TRUNC(-8.9)=-8 truncation-toward-zero. That is precisely the semantic nuance that separates Excel's INT from TRUNC, and it's already encoded and tested here. Given Q8.8 is this library's established representation tier for decimal/real numbers (not a one-off), q_to_int_i16 is the direct match for INT(number) where number lives in that tier. (For the checked-integer tier INT is trivial identity since those values are already whole; no f32-tier floor-to-int cast cell exists, but Q8.8 is the tier Excel-compatibility packs actually use for fractional quantities, so that gap doesn't change the classification.)

entries.name: ISO.CEILING
entries.description: Returns a number rounded up to the nearest integer or multiple of significance
entries.repr: fixed-point Q8.8, signed (i16) — a new kernel alongside the existing signed Q8.8 lineage (int_to_q8_i16, q_mul_i16, q_div_i16, q_to_int_i16) in the fixed-point pack, chosen over checked-int because ISO.CEILING's real-world use (rounding to a fractional significance like 0.05) needs a fractional step, which u16/u32 checked-int can't represent; a lower-fidelity checked-int sign-magnitude tier (mirroring smag_div/smag_cmp) would only cover the integer-significance subset. New logic needed: ceil(x, significance) = sign-independent round toward +positive infinity to the nearest multiple of |significance| (not "away from zero" — the specific ISO.CEILING/CEILING.MATH convention that differs from plain CEILING's same-sign requirement), using div_ceil_u32's q+1-if-remainder idiom generalized to a signed dividend, plus the significance==0 or number==0 -> 0 domain rule.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is ISO.CEILING(number, [significance]): number can be any real (often fractional, e.g. rounding a price to the nearest 0.05) and negative, significance defaults to 1 and its sign is ignored, and the defining rule (shared with CEILING.MATH, distinct from the old CEILING) is that rounding always goes toward +infinity regardless of the sign of number. The library's nearest sibling, `snap_up`/`snap_up_u32` (bit-mask/checked-arithmetic, "Round x UP to the nearest multiple of step"), only covers unsigned integers with an integer step — it has no sign to get "regardless of sign" right and no fractional-significance domain at all, so per the NPV-correction precedent (classify against the real signature, not a narrower sibling) this isn't covered. It also isn't cleanly composable: no pair of existing cell outputs glues into a signed, fractional-step, sign-of-significance-ignored ceiling-to-multiple — `div_ceil_u32` (checked-arithmetic) only ceils a plain quotient, and `frac_of_whole_ceil` (fractions) computes ceil(n/d*whole), a different shape (scaling a whole by a fraction, not snapping to an arbitrary step). This is a small, distinct new kernel, not glue, so it's a `candidate`.

entries.name: LCM
entries.description: Returns the least common multiple
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: lcm (run(a,b) -> u16) and lcm3 (run(a,b,c) -> u16) for the fixed-arity cases; arbitrary arity = host folds by calling lcm repeatedly: acc = lcm(acc, next). Wide/checked siblings lcm_u32 (LcmChecked::run) and lcm3_u32 (Lcm3Checked::run) available if wider domain/overflow-checking is needed.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is LCM(number1, [number2], ..., [number255]) -- arbitrary arity, same shape as GCD. cell80 already has exact fixed-arity siblings: `lcm` (run(a,b) -> u16, 2-arg, u16 domain), `lcm3` (run(a,b,c) -> u16, 3-arg), plus wide/checked variants `lcm_u32` (LcmChecked::run, escalates on overflow) and `lcm3_u32` (Lcm3Checked::run, lcm(lcm(a,b),c) chained). Per the no-fixed-arity-doesn't-mean-covered rule, these don't make arbitrary-arity LCM 'covered'. But unlike NPV (host_only, because each cash-flow term is independently weighted and needs simultaneous array-state), LCM is a plain associative/commutative fold: lcm(a,b,c,d,...) = lcm(lcm(lcm(a,b),c),d)... This is exactly the caller-runs-them-in-sequence form of composable named in the brief -- the host repeatedly calls the existing 2-arg `lcm` cell, feeding the running result back in as one operand alongside the next number, no array-state field or new cell required. Neither composable-author reason applies on top of that: reason 1 (well-known/expected) is already satisfied by the existing `lcm`/`lcm3`/`lcm_u32`/`lcm3_u32` family naming the operation at its common fixed arities, so there's no naming gap left to fill; reason 2 (genuine complexity) doesn't apply since the arbitrary-arity extension is pure fold/glue, not a new algorithm. Default composable-skip stands.

entries.name: MDETERM
entries.description: Returns the matrix determinant of an array
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: null (no existing id returns a standalone NxN determinant for N=3; matrix_det_2x2 only covers N=2)
entries.repr: f32 (IEEE binary32) throughout, fixed 3x3 arity -- following matrix_solve_3x3's exact precedent (docs/cell-index.md:546): a native-integer 3-term-deep cofactor expansion (three 2x2 minors, each itself a product-of-products) would blow past even a widened u32 kernel, which is the same reasoning that pushed matrix_solve_3x3 to f32 instead of an exact signed-fraction result. New logic needed: expose the standard 3x3 cofactor expansion det = a11*(a22*a33-a23*a32) - a12*(a21*a33-a23*a31) + a13*(a21*a32-a22*a31) as its own standalone output -- currently this exact computation is only ever inlined inside MatrixSolve3x3 and never returned on its own.
entries.missing_capability: null (candidate, not host_only, for the fixed-3x3 case; true arbitrary-N generality would need array/range-typed cell inputs, which CellHost's scalar-only, non-round-tripping state model does not support -- same array-state-field gap already documented for NPV)
entries.reason: Excel's MDETERM(array) computes the determinant of a square matrix of ARBITRARY size (2x2, 3x3, 4x4, ...) supplied as a single array/range argument. cell80's matrix pack only has fixed-arity, named-scalar-field determinant support: `matrix_det_2x2` (docs/cell-index.md:432, `a*d - b*c`) covers exactly N=2. There is no standalone N=3 determinant cell -- `matrix_solve_3x3` (docs/cell-index.md:546, lives in cells/numerical-primitives/) computes 3x3 cofactor-expansion determinants internally (det(A) and 3 column-substituted variants) to feed Cramer's-rule division, but that's an inlined intermediate value never exposed as MatrixSolve3x3's own output, and cells cannot call each other to expose it externally. So MDETERM is not `covered` (2x2 case only), and it is not `composable-skip`/`composable-author` either -- gluing existing outputs can't produce it: there is no existing cell whose output IS a 3x3 determinant to glue, and reproducing the cofactor expansion from scratch is exactly the "genuine complexity, not simple glue" case the taxonomy doc's reason-2 caveat says belongs in `candidate`, not `composable-author` (mirrors the IRR/RATE worked example in docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 4). Excel's true arbitrary-N array signature is beyond what named-scalar-field cells can ever represent generically (the array-state-field gap: CellHost's runner only round-trips fixed named scalars, never a variable-length/variable-shape array), so full MDETERM is not attainable at any N -- but the library's own established precedent is to stop at a fixed 3x3 ceiling (matrix_solve_3x3 already made this exact tradeoff, and matrix pack's README notes 2x2 is "the vector floor exception to the matrix non-goal" extended only that far). A standalone `matrix_det_3x3` cell -- 9 named f32 coefficients a11..a33, standard 3-term cofactor expansion, single f32 output -- is the natural next fixed-arity candidate, filling the gap between the already-shipped `matrix_det_2x2` and the already-shipped `matrix_solve_3x3`'s internal-only 3x3 determinant.

entries.name: MINVERSE
entries.description: Returns the matrix inverse of an array
entries.repr: candidate, fixed small arity matching matrix_solve_3x3's precedent: primary cell matrix_inverse_2x2 as an exact signed fraction (4 entries sharing one positive denominator = det, mirroring matrix_solve_2x2's div-by-det convention with sign-magnitude tracking); optional matrix_inverse_3x3 sibling in IEEE binary32 mirroring matrix_solve_3x3's cofactor-expansion/f32 tier. New logic needed beyond existing matrix cells: adjugate construction (diagonal swap + off-diagonal negation for 2x2; transpose-of-cofactor-matrix for 3x3) plus a 4-way (or 9-way) division sharing one denominator -- no existing cell produces more than 2 divided outputs from one determinant.
entries.reason:
Not covered: the matrix pack (7 cells, docs/cell-index.md line 427) has matrix_det_2x2, matrix_trace_2x2, matrix_frobenius_norm_sq_2x2, matrix_real_eigenvalues_2x2, matrix_solve_2x2, matrix_mul_2x2, matrix_apply_2x2, plus matrix_solve_3x3 (line 546) elsewhere -- none of these produces a full inverse matrix (a grep for "invers" across cell-index.md turns up only unrelated inverse-direction cells like mod_inverse, DOLLARFR/DOLLARDE, arithmetic_term_index -- nothing matrix-shaped).

Excel's real signature, MINVERSE(array), takes one square array of arbitrary size (2x2, 3x3, ... NxN up to sheet limits) -- at that full generality it's host_only for the same reason NPV was corrected to host_only in the taxonomy amendment: arbitrary-size array arguments don't round-trip across a cell80 call boundary (Runner zeros state each run()).

But the library already has a working convention for this exact situation: matrix_solve_3x3 (line 546) is explicitly framed as "extending matrix_solve_2x2... to one more dimension" via 9 named f32 scalar coefficients (a11..a33) plus 3 RHS values -- a fixed-arity, Excel-function-shaped sibling, not a claim to cover arbitrary N. Following that same precedent, the actionable next cell is a fixed matrix_inverse_2x2 (exact signed fraction, shared denominator = det, mirroring matrix_solve_2x2's own div-by-det pattern) with a matrix_inverse_3x3 f32 sibling analogous to matrix_solve_3x3. This is not composable-skip/author from matrix_det_2x2 + existing divides: it requires the adjugate sign-pattern (swap diagonal + negate off-diagonal for 2x2; transpose-of-cofactor-matrix for 3x3) applied across 4 (or 9) output entries sharing one denominator -- a genuinely new multi-output shape distinct from every existing matrix cell (det/trace/frobenius are single scalars; matrix_solve_2x2 is a 2-output Cramer's-rule vector solve, not a full matrix; matrix_mul_2x2 is pure multiply-accumulate with no division or sign-flip pattern at all). So: candidate at fixed 2x2/3x3 arity following matrix_solve_3x3's precedent; the unbounded-N case stays host_only (array-state-field gap) if taken at Excel's literal generality.

entries.name: MMULT
entries.description: Returns the matrix product of two arrays
entries.missing_capability: Two-sided array I/O across the cell call boundary: (1) arbitrary-shape array *inputs* (M×N, N×P) -- the array-state-field gap already confirmed for NPV/IRR/holidays-array; (2) a data-dependent-size array *output* (M×P result matrix) -- no cell80 cell can vary its number of output state fields based on runtime input dimensions, since fields are fixed at author time.
entries.reason: Excel's MMULT(array1, array2) multiplies arbitrary-shape M×N and N×P arrays into a full M×P result array. The matrix pack (7 cells: matrix_apply_2x2, matrix_det_2x2, matrix_frobenius_norm_sq_2x2, matrix_mul_2x2, matrix_real_eigenvalues_2x2, matrix_solve_2x2, matrix_trace_2x2) plus matrix_solve_3x3 (numerical-primitives pack) covers only fixed-size 2x2 (and one 3x3 linear-solve) shapes -- matrix_mul_2x2 handles exactly the degenerate 2x2*2x2 case, which per the NPV-correction precedent (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md) does not count as coverage of an arbitrary-arity real signature. MMULT hits the array-state-field gap on BOTH sides: arbitrary-size array inputs (the same gap that made NPV/IRR/NETWORKDAYS's holidays-array host_only) AND, worse, a data-dependent-size array OUTPUT (an M×P matrix, not a scalar) -- cell80 state fields are fixed in count at author time and cannot vary with input dimensions, a strictly harder problem than any variadic-input case already refused. docs/library-growth.md's wave-13 note also documents an explicit matrix non-goal ('no general NxN solver, just the 2x2 floor'), with matrix_solve_3x3 the sole, specifically-motivated exception -- MMULT is precisely the general-NxN operation that non-goal targets, and even a fixed 3x3 variant would only dodge the arithmetic complexity, not the actual blocker (variable output shape).

entries.name: MOD
entries.description: Returns the remainder from division
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: div_i16 + mul_i16 + sub_i16 (truncated remainder r = a - div_i16(a,b)*b) corrected via same_sign_i16(r, b) to add b back when signs disagree and r != 0 -- yields Excel's exact MOD(number, divisor) divisor-sign convention over the i16 domain
entries.composable_author_reason: well-known-expected (MOD is a top-tier well-known Excel function; the divisor-sign remainder convention is a classic, easy-to-get-wrong convention-fragility case, not merely "expected to exist")
entries.repr: checked-int, i16 signed domain (sign-magnitude style, matching div_i16/mul_i16/sub_i16/same_sign_i16's existing convention) -- not f32, since the decisive well-known gotcha (negative-operand sign convention) is an integer-domain concern; non-integer real-number MOD support would be a separate f32 extension not addressed here
entries.reason: Excel MOD(number, divisor) = number - divisor*INT(number/divisor), whose real signature includes negative operands with the well-known "remainder takes the sign of the divisor" convention (e.g. MOD(-7,3)=2, MOD(7,-3)=-2) -- distinct from a plain truncating remainder. cell80's existing unsigned remainder cells (`safe_mod`, `mod_u32` -- docs/cell-index.md lines 719, 176) are u16/u32-only and structurally cannot represent a negative dividend or divisor at all, so they are not "covered": MOD's real signature is not the always-nonnegative case those cells encode. It is, however, composable from already-shipped signed i16 primitives: `div_i16` (truncated quotient, line 785) + `mul_i16` (line 791) + `sub_i16` (line 794) give the truncating remainder r = a - q*b (same sign as the dividend, matching Rust's native `%`); `same_sign_i16` (line 639) then supplies the one conditional check needed to detect when that truncated remainder must be corrected (add b back when r != 0 and sign(r) != sign(b)) to land on Excel's actual divisor-sign convention. That's a bounded, non-iterative composition (no convergence loop, no multi-valued case analysis) -- the same shape as the gcd_u32 precedent (a loop over already-existing mod/compare primitives), not the IRR/RATE "algorithm wearing a composable disguise" shape -- so reason 2 does not apply and this isn't a candidate misclassification. Reason 1 applies cleanly: MOD is one of Excel's best-known functions, and the divisor-sign convention is exactly the kind of thing "easy to get subtly wrong re-deriving by hand each time" (the taxonomy doc's own phrasing) that a canonical cell earns its keep encoding once, tested -- worth authoring despite being technically composable. (Excel's MOD also accepts non-integer real numbers; that f32/real-domain slice is a separate, lower-priority extension not required to justify this classification -- the integer signed-divisor-convention case alone already clears reason 1.)

entries.name: MROUND
entries.description: Returns a number rounded to the desired multiple
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: Composes from round_to_multiple / round_to_multiple_u32 (ties-away-from-zero magnitude rounding, cell-index.md:107-108) via: sign(number)==sign(multiple) check -> escalate/#NUM! if mismatched and both nonzero; else round_to_multiple(|number|, |multiple|) then reapply the shared sign; multiple==0 short-circuits to 0 (overriding round_to_multiple's own "x if step==0" identity default). A new excel_mround cell would inline this the same way excel_dollarfr inlines num_digits' loop and excel_effect inlines compound_increase_by_bps's technique (cells can't call cells).
entries.composable_author_reason: well-known/expected functionality (reason 1) — MROUND is a commonly-used, named Excel operation, and its sign-mismatch #NUM! rule plus its multiple==0 special case are convention-fragility details (the latter directly inverting round_to_multiple's own step==0 default) that are easy to get subtly wrong re-deriving by hand each time.
entries.repr: checked-int tier (u16/u32 magnitude via round_to_multiple/round_to_multiple_u32, signed handling via a sign-compare case-split in the style already used for i16 sign predicates like is_negative_i16, cell-index.md:627) — same integer/bps-scaled representation convention used for excel_effect and excel_dollarfr rather than a literal f32 MROUND, consistent with existing Excel80 precedent.
entries.reason: Excel MROUND(number, multiple) = "round number to the nearest multiple of multiple, ties away from zero; #NUM! if number and multiple have different (nonzero) signs; multiple==0 -> 0." The core magnitude algorithm already exists verbatim: `round_to_multiple` (docs/cell-index.md:107, u16) and `round_to_multiple_u32` (line 108, wide sibling) round x to the NEAREST multiple of step with ties rounding up -- for nonnegative operands "ties up" IS "ties away from zero," so abs(number) vs abs(multiple) through round_to_multiple/round_to_multiple_u32 reproduces MROUND's real result exactly once resigned (verified by hand: MROUND(-9,-6) = -12 away-from-zero == -(round_to_multiple(9,6)=12)). That's a straight composition of one existing cell's output. What isn't free glue is the Excel-specific edge behavior around it: (a) the sign-mismatch check that turns into a #NUM! error, which round_to_multiple has no notion of, and (b) the multiple==0 case, where MROUND returns 0 but round_to_multiple's own convention is "x if step == 0" -- the exact opposite identity default. Both are the kind of fragile, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong-by-hand convention the taxonomy amendment's reason 1 calls out (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 2, reason 1), the same argument already used to justify `excel_effect`'s divide-then-compound-then-subtract ordering and `excel_dollarfr`'s rounding convention (cell-index.md:301-302) as composable-author rather than composable-skip. MROUND is also a genuinely well-known, frequently-used named Excel function (reason 1's baseline test), not an obscure alias -- so this clears composable-author, not composable-skip.

entries.name: MUNIT
entries.description: Returns the unit matrix or the specified dimension
entries.missing_capability: Dimension-parameterized (runtime-sized) array output. cell80's ABI fixes a cell's output shape at compile time as named struct fields (matrix_solve_3x3's x1/x2/x3 is the precedent for how multiple named scalars round-trip -- but that arity is baked in at authoring time, never a runtime argument). MUNIT(dimension) takes dimension as a call-time value and must return a dimension x dimension array whose size varies with it -- there is no mechanism for a cell's output field count to scale with an input value. This is the output-side counterpart of the array-state-field gap that made NPV host_only (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's correction note): NPV can't take an arbitrary-length input list, MUNIT can't produce an arbitrary-size output array; both fail for the same underlying reason (no variable-length array round-trip across the run() boundary).
entries.reason: Confirmed via docs/cell-index.md: the matrix pack (7 cells -- matrix_apply_2x2, matrix_det_2x2, matrix_frobenius_norm_sq_2x2, matrix_mul_2x2, matrix_real_eigenvalues_2x2, matrix_solve_2x2, matrix_trace_2x2) plus matrix_solve_3x3 (numerical-primitives pack) contain no identity/unit-matrix cell, and a repo-wide grep for identity/unit_matrix/munit/eye( turns up nothing relevant. MUNIT isn't composable either: it takes no existing matrix as input to glue outputs from -- it's a pure generator keyed only on a dimension scalar, so composable-skip/composable-author don't apply (nothing to compose). It also isn't a good candidate: per the amendment's own NPV correction, a fixed-arity sibling (e.g. a hardcoded munit_2 or munit_3 returning constants 1/0/0/1) does not cover Excel's real MUNIT(dimension) signature, where dimension is a runtime argument setting the output size -- and unlike matrix_solve_3x3 (a real Cramer's-rule computation fixed at n=3 by design), a fixed-n identity generator has zero computational content (just compile-time constants), so there's no genuine kernel to bound into a candidate row. The actual blocker is architectural: cell80 has no way to size a cell's output array by a runtime dimension argument, which routes this to host_only rather than candidate or out_of_scope.

entries.name: ODD
entries.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest odd integer
entries.repr: f32 (softfloat tier) -- single scalar argument, analogous to lerp_f32/norm2_f32/excel_dollarfr/matrix_solve_3x3's f32 family rather than checked-arithmetic's whole-number-only rounding kernels or fixed-point's Q8.8 scale.
entries.reason: No existing cell80 cell computes ODD's real behavior: round a (possibly fractional, possibly negative) number AWAY FROM ZERO to the nearest odd integer (ODD(0)=1 by Excel convention). Searched docs/cell-index.md for rounding kernels: checked-arithmetic's round_to_multiple/round_to_multiple_u32, snap_down/snap_down_u32, snap_up/snap_up_u32, ceil_div, div_ceil_u32, div_floor_u32, round_div/round_div_checked_u32 all round an UNSIGNED integer to a caller-chosen step/multiple -- none target 'nearest odd integer' and none handle a negative or fractional input's away-from-zero direction. predicates' is_odd/is_odd_u32/is_even/is_even_u32 only classify the parity of an ALREADY-integral value; they don't round anything, so they can't glue-compose into ODD by themselves. No excel_odd/excel_even cell exists (grepped, none found), unlike excel-financial's excel_oddfyield/excel_oddlyield which are unrelated (bond odd-coupon-period pricing, not this Math&Trig rounding function). Since Excel's ODD accepts any real number (fractional inputs round outward too, e.g. ODD(1.3)=3), and cell80's checked-arithmetic/number-theory packs work over already-whole u16/u32 domains, this doesn't fit the checked-int tier cleanly -- it fits the f32 (softfloat) tier already used for single/small-arity real-valued cells (lerp_f32, norm2_f32, excel_dollarfr's manual half-away-from-zero rounding, matrix_solve_3x3's f32 family). New logic needed: (1) sign-aware round-away-from-zero to an integer (fceil for x>=0, ffloor-equivalent negation trick for x<0, using the ffloor/fceil/ftrunc softfloat kernels rustz80/src/softfloat.rs already implements as host primitives -- not yet exposed as a standalone callable cell), (2) a parity check on that integer, (3) if even, step by 1 further away from zero to reach the next odd integer, (4) the x==0 special case forcing output 1. This is a small, bounded case-analysis algorithm (sign branch + parity branch), not an iteration/convergence loop, so per the taxonomy's reason-2 self-check (real algorithmic complexity usually means candidate, not composable-author) this is correctly a candidate rather than composable-author: there are no two existing cells whose outputs could simply be glued (no existing 'round away from zero' cell and no existing 'bump to nearest odd' cell to feed each other).

entries.name: POWER
entries.description: Returns the result of a number raised to a power
entries.missing_capability: Transcendental exp/ln (or an equivalent general fractional/real-exponent pow) in the softfloat f32 tier -- rustz80/src/softfloat.rs's kernel set (fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/feq/flt/fle/int_to_f32/q16_to_f32/f32_to_int_trunc/f32_to_q16/ftrunc/ffloor/fceil/fround/fmin/fmax) has no fpow/fexp/fln entry, and none of nth_root_f32/pow_small/pow_checked_u32/frac_pow/pow_mod/pow_mod_u32 evaluate base^y for an arbitrary caller-supplied real y.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is POWER(number, power) with `power` an arbitrary real (fractional and/or negative, e.g. POWER(8,2.5), POWER(2,-0.5)) -- not restricted to a whole-number exponent. Every existing power-shaped cell in cell80 only covers the whole-number-exponent case: pow_small (u16 base^exp, saturating), pow_checked_u32 (checked exact u32 base^exp), pow_mod/pow_mod_u32 (modular base^exp mod m), frac_pow (fraction^whole-k), pow_equals_u32 (verifies claimed whole power). nth_root_f32 looks adjacent but solves the *inverse* problem for a caller-fixed whole exponent n (finds x with x^n=c via Newton seeded from sqrt) -- it is not a forward base^(arbitrary real y) evaluator, and every financial cell that leans on it (excel_db, excel_nominal, excel_rate's cousins, excel_oddfyield) explicitly notes it exists precisely *because* no fractional-exponent pow is available, routing around the gap rather than closing it. Genuinely computing x^y for arbitrary real y needs exp(y*ln(x)) (or an equivalent series), i.e. a transcendental exp/ln pair. Grepping rustz80/src/softfloat.rs confirms the f32 tier's complete kernel set is only fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/feq/flt/fle/int_to_f32/q16_to_f32/f32_to_int_trunc/f32_to_q16/ftrunc/ffloor/fceil/fround/fmin/fmax -- no fpow, no fexp, no fln, no fsin/fcos. Per the task background, transcendentals (including pow-with-fractional-exponent) are a confirmed non-goal, so this is host_only, not candidate-at-f32-tier and not composable-author via nth_root_f32 (that cell answers a different question -- a fixed-n root, not an arbitrary caller-supplied real exponent). Missing capability: a transcendental exp/ln primitive (or a general real-exponent pow built on one) in the softfloat/f32 tier -- absent by design, matching math-server-map.md's own host_only reasons ("needs floats/transcendentals ... the dialect's permanent non-goals").

entries.name: QUOTIENT
entries.description: Returns the integer portion of a division
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: div_floor_u32 (checked-arithmetic, u32, wide/escalating tier); safe_div (safe-arith, u16, zero-on-b==0 tier) -- either already covers QUOTIENT's core semantics depending on desired width/error convention
entries.repr: checked-int: u32 (div_floor_u32) or u16 (safe_div) -- both unsigned, matching Excel QUOTIENT's truncate-toward-zero behavior exactly since truncation == floor for nonnegative operands
entries.reason: QUOTIENT(numerator, denominator) = "integer portion of a division", i.e. truncate(a/b). Over the library's unsigned-integer domain, truncation and floor are the same operation (no sign to truncate toward), so this is already shipped twice, at two width tiers: `div_floor_u32` in checked-arithmetic ("Floor division of two u32 values: a / b, rounded down" -- its own state field is literally named `quotient`, escalating needs_wider_math on b==0 instead of Excel's #DIV/0!), and `safe_div` in safe-arith ("Integer divide a / b, returning 0 when b == 0" -- u16, free-fn signature, closer to Excel's plain two-arg call shape). Both compute exactly what QUOTIENT computes for nonnegative operands; they differ only in their b==0 convention (escalate vs. return 0), a corner-case error-handling choice, not a missing capability. No new cell composes or is needed -- this is a rename/alias situation, not composable-skip (an existing cell doesn't just compose to the answer, it already *is* the answer) and not composable-author (no fragile convention or algorithm to encode beyond what's already shipped). Excel's real signature only takes two scalar args (numerator, denominator) -- no array-state-field gap here, unlike NPV/SUM-family functions.

entries.name: RADIANS
entries.description: Converts degrees to radians
entries.repr: fixed-point (Q8.8), following the geom_circle_area_approx / geom_circle_circumference_approx fixed-pi-constant precedent (small fixed-arity single-input cell, matrix_solve_3x3-style precedent for a distinct new tiny cell)
entries.reason: No cell converts degrees to radians -- grepping cell-index.md for radian/degree/pi turns up nothing except two circle cells. The only place pi lives in the library today is baked as an inline literal inside `geom_circle_area_approx` (area = (r*r*804)>>8, 804 = round(pi*256) in Q8.8) and `geom_circle_circumference_approx` ((r*1608)>>8, 1608=2*804) -- neither exposes pi as a reusable output, so there is no existing-cell composition to glue this from (rules out composable-skip/composable-author). RADIANS itself needs no transcendental (it's just degrees * pi / 180, a scalar multiply by a constant), so it's within reach of the same fixed-point tier those two cells already established -- but it needs its own new kernel (radians_q8 = (degrees * 804) / 180 at wide u32 width, the same widen-then-divide discipline q_div/geom_circle_circumference_approx already use), not a glue of existing outputs.

entries.name: DEGREES
entries.description: Converts radians to degrees
entries.repr: f32 (softfloat tier), matching the precedent of lerp_f32/norm2_f32/clamp_f32 (softfloat pack) and matrix_solve_3x3/nth_root_f32 (numerical-primitives pack) -- new logic is a single constant multiply (radians * 180/pi) via the existing fmul softfloat kernel, no iteration or case analysis needed.
entries.reason: No cell anywhere converts between radians and degrees, and no cell represents an angle in radians at all — grepped cell-index.md for radian/degree/angle/atan/bearing and the only angle-adjacent hits are orientation2d/cos_frac_from_sides, which stay in cross-product/law-of-cosines fraction space and never touch radians. DEGREES is a single scalar multiply by the constant 180/pi, but the only exposed generic multiply-by-constant primitive in the library is the fixed-point q_mul (Q8.8, run(a:u16,b:u16)->u16) — its i16-backed Q8.8 domain caps magnitude at roughly +/-128, far too narrow for Excel's real DEGENERATE domain (arbitrary-magnitude reals, e.g. thousands of accumulated radians), so it can't actually compose this at adequate range/precision. No generic scalar fmul_f32 cell is exposed either (softfloat's fmul kernel is only ever used internal to composed formulas like lerp_f32/norm2_f32/clamp_f32/matrix_solve_3x3/nth_root_f32), so there is no existing cell whose output can be chained to produce a real Excel-compatible answer -- it fails the composable test on representation grounds, not just as a style choice. It is genuinely tiny and new logic needed is minimal: one f32 multiply (radians * 57.29577951..., or equivalently divide by pi/180) through the already-owned softfloat kernel, the same shape as the numerical-primitives/softfloat pack's existing new-formula cells.

entries.name: ROMAN
entries.description: Converts an Arabic numeral to Roman, as text
entries.missing_capability: str_out promotion / bounded string output (Phase S2/S3 of docs/11-machine-text.md) -- confirmed not yet shipped ("S2/S3 ... stay gated behind the 1K scale curve and the admission gate"); only S0/S1 (ABI v3 str[N]/bytes[N] manifest types, &str INPUT params, byte literals) are shipped. No cell in the 718-cell library (docs/cell-index.md) has ever returned anything but u16.
entries.reason: ROMAN's entire job is to produce Roman-numeral TEXT ("MCMXCIX"), not a number. The greedy-subtraction algorithm itself is trivial glue over a 13-entry value table (1000=M,900=CM,...,1=I) and would be cheap to write against number-theory's div/mod primitives -- but every one of the 718 cells in docs/cell-index.md returns `-> u16` with no exception (verified by grep across the whole index), because the dialect has no cell that can emit a multi-character string as output. docs/11-machine-text.md confirms this directly: it defines Phase S for "machine text," and its own status line says "S0 and S1 shipped" (ABI v3 manifest types, `&str` *input* params, byte literals, `[u8;N]` fields) while "S2/S3 (the string packs and `str_out` promotion) stay gated behind the 1K scale curve and the admission gate." `str_out` promotion -- the mechanism that would let a cell build a bounded output buffer and have the host promote it to a real string at the boundary (section 2.3/section 9 of that doc) -- is exactly what ROMAN needs and exactly what is NOT yet landed. This isn't the array-state-field gap or the transcendentals gap named in docs/excel-financial-map.md; it's a third, distinct missing capability (string OUTPUT), and Excel's own ROMAN is the clearest possible function to trip it since unlike number_to_base (which fakes a "base conversion" by reassembling digits into a decimal literal -- still a u16 number) Roman numerals use letters (M/D/C/L/X/V/I) that cannot be smuggled back into a numeric return value at all.

entries.name: ARABIC
entries.description: Converts a Roman number to Arabic, as a number
entries.missing_capability: No string/text input type in the 16-bit register calling convention (confirmed dialect-wide, cited in excel_networkdays_intl's own docstring), combined with the already-documented array-state-field gap (CellHost's runner zeros state each run(), so an arbitrary-length argument list -- here, a variable-length Roman-numeral character sequence -- cannot round-trip across a call boundary).
entries.reason: ARABIC(text) takes a Roman-numeral STRING (e.g. "MCMXCIV") and must be parsed character-by-character with a subtractive-notation rule (a smaller numeral before a larger one subtracts, e.g. "IV"=4, "IX"=9). Two separate capability gaps block this, neither of which any existing pack works around: (1) the calling convention has no string/text type at all — this is stated directly in cell-index.md's own docstring for excel_networkdays_intl, which chose a bitmask encoding over a string argument "since the dialect has no strings"; (2) even if the numerals were pre-split into character codes, the input is variable-length (Roman numerals run from 1 character, "I", to 15 for "MMMDCCCLXXXVIII"=3888, and Excel's real ARABIC doesn't even cap length before erroring) — this is exactly the array-state-field gap already confirmed project-wide: CellHost's runner zeros state every run(), so an arbitrary-length argument list never round-trips across a call boundary. Grepped cell-index.md for "roman"/"arabic": zero hits. No pack (number-theory, checked-arithmetic, packing-bcd, bit-encoding, etc.) has any char/string/text-parsing cell to build on -- packing-bcd's bcd_encode/bcd_decode family is fixed 2-or-4-digit BINARY<->BCD conversion, not numeral-letter parsing, and offers no glue path. Unlike matrix_solve_3x3 (candidate precedent: fixed-arity numeric inputs, just more of them), there is no fixed small arity to pin ARABIC to, because Roman-numeral length genuinely varies with the value being represented -- so this isn't a "candidate, pick a tier" row either. Missing capability: a string/text input type in the calling convention, and/or a variable-length-argument round-trip mechanism across the call boundary.

entries.name: BASE
entries.description: Converts a number into a text representation with the given radix (base)
entries.missing_capability: Text/string return type (dialect has no string ABI value — cells only return numeric u16/i16). Escalation code 0xFF01 `needs_strings` already exists precisely for this gap (cell80/src/report.rs:31, docs/09-cell80-abi.md:124, docs/10-dialect-semantics.md:401), confirming it is a real, named, unbuilt capability rather than a hand-wave.
entries.reason: Excel BASE(number, radix, [min_length]) converts number to a TEXT representation in the given radix (2-36), left-padded with leading zeros to min_length. cell80 has a superficially similar cell -- `number_to_base` (docs/cell-index.md) -- but it is not the same function: it only covers radix 2-9 and reassembles the base-b digits as a base-10 *numeric* display value (e.g. n=13,base=2 -> the decimal literal 1101), never producing an actual string. That reassembly trick fundamentally cannot generalize to Excel's real signature: (1) radix 10-36 needs letter digits (A-Z for values 10-35), which have no numeric reassembly at all; (2) min_length's leading-zero padding is only meaningful on a string -- "00111" as a number silently collapses to 111, losing exactly the behavior Excel documents. So even the radix<=9, no-padding slice of BASE isn't truly covered by number_to_base once min_length is in scope, since Excel's min_length has no default that makes it droppable (it's optional but changes output when supplied). Also checked num_digits_base (counts base-b digit width, doesn't emit digits) and bcd_encode/bcd_encode16 (fixed nibble packing, not arbitrary-radix) -- neither is closer. No amount of gluing 1-2 existing cells' numeric outputs produces a text string with letter digits and zero-padding; the blocker is the missing string/text return capability itself (same 0xFF01 `needs_strings` wall the taxonomy doc already names, not a new algorithmic gap and not array-state). Classifying as host_only rather than candidate because the representation gap -- not the arithmetic (which is trivial: repeated divide-by-radix, exactly what number_to_base and num_digits_base already do internally) -- is what blocks this function.

entries.name: ROUND
entries.description: Rounds a number to a specified number of digits
entries.repr: f32 tier (matching excel_dollarfr's own tier and reusing its proven technique): ExcelRound::run(value: f32, num_digits: i16) -> f32-ish u16 result, small-arity like matrix_solve_3x3's precedent. New logic needed: (1) build 10^|num_digits| via a bounded repeated-multiply loop (num_digits over a small fixed range, e.g. -10..=10, to stay in f32 range), (2) scale value by that power (multiply if num_digits >= 0, divide if negative -- or the inverse depending on which direction is scaled first), (3) a new round-to-nearest-integer-half-away-from-zero f32 primitive (does not exist in softfloat.rs today -- fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt only), (4) scale back by dividing/multiplying by the same power. Escalate on non-finite input/output the same way drag_force_f32/kinetic_energy_f32/verlet_step_f32 do.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is ROUND(number, num_digits) over arbitrary reals with num_digits positive (decimal places), negative (tens/hundreds/...), or zero -- a decimal power-of-ten rescale plus round-half-away-from-zero, then rescale back. Nothing in cell80 covers this: `round_to_multiple`/`round_to_multiple_u32`/`snap_down`/`snap_up`/`round_div`/`round_div_checked_u32`/`percent_round` (checked-arithmetic pack, cited in docs/cell-index.md) are all integer/u16-u32 domain with an integer *step* parameter -- they can express "round to nearest 10/100" (negative num_digits over whole numbers) but not positive-num_digits decimal-place rounding of a fractional value, and none operate on f32. The softfloat/f32 tier (rustz80/src/softfloat.rs) has only fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt -- no round-to-nearest-integer f32 primitive and no power-of-ten helper exist as standalone, reusable cells. The one place cell80 already built this exact technique -- power-of-ten scaling via a repeated-multiply loop, plus round-half-away-from-zero tie-breaking -- is inlined inside `excel_dollarfr` (docs/cell-index.md line 301: "numerator=ROUND(remainder*fraction) rounded half-away-from-zero ... turned into a power-of-ten divisor via a repeated-multiply loop"), but that logic is private to DOLLARFR's own call (cells can't call each other) and only handles one fixed internal sub-step, not a general two-argument ROUND(value, num_digits) with a sign-varying exponent. Since gluing existing cells' outputs can't produce this (no exposed pow10 cell, no exposed f32 round-to-int cell), and building it requires new algorithmic logic (signed-exponent power-of-ten loop + a new round-half-away-from-zero f32 kernel), this is a candidate, not composable-author -- matching the taxonomy amendment's IRR/RATE precedent (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md Part 4): a function that looks glue-composable at a glance but is actually an algorithm wearing a composable disguise gets filed as candidate. Reason 1 (well-known/expected, with real convention fragility -- half-away-from-zero tie-breaking is easy to get subtly wrong) supports authoring it once built, but the classification itself is candidate because the composition doesn't exist yet.

entries.name: ROUNDDOWN
entries.description: Rounds a number down, toward zero
entries.repr: checked-int / signed sign-magnitude (i16), the same convention `div_i16` and `mul_i16` already use, generalized with a digit-count-to-power-of-ten scale factor.
entries.reason: No existing cell80 id covers ROUNDDOWN(number, num_digits) -- confirmed no `rounddown`/`roundup`/`excel_round*`/`trunc`/`mround` id anywhere in docs/cell-index.md (only `excel_dollarfr`, an unrelated bond-price cell, touches a similar digits-to-power-of-ten technique). It also isn't a clean 1-2-cell composable-skip/author case across Excel's real signature, because the existing rounding kernels split along an axis ROUNDDOWN needs unified: `round_to_multiple` (id 107), `snap_down`/`snap_down_u32` (109/110), `snap_up`/`snap_up_u32` (111/112), `round_div` (717), `div_ceil_u32` (162), `div_floor_u32` (164) are all unsigned (u16/u32) and floor/ceil-to-a-caller-supplied-arbitrary-step -- none truncate toward zero for negative inputs, which is exactly the FLOOR-vs-ROUNDDOWN distinction that matters for Excel's negative-number case (ROUNDDOWN(-17,-1) = -10, not -20 as a floor-based snap_down would give). `div_i16` (785) already truncates toward zero via sign-magnitude, matching ROUNDDOWN's direction, but has no digit-count/power-of-10 concept at all -- it's a plain a/b divide. And Excel's num_digits can be positive (decimal places, needing a fractional-number representation) as well as negative (tens/hundreds), so a full-signature cell must also decide a number representation (Q8.8 binary fixed-point doesn't decompose cleanly into decimal digits; the exact-fraction pack's `frac_of_whole_floor` (365) floors an unsigned n/d*whole but has no sign handling either). Building this needs genuinely new logic, not glue: sign-magnitude decompose the input (div_i16/mul_i16's pattern), compute 10^|num_digits| via a repeated-multiply loop (precedented inline in `excel_dollarfr`'s digits-to-power-of-ten step, id 301, but never exposed as its own reusable cell), then truncate-toward-zero at that scale (divide, floor the magnitude, multiply back) with the multiply/divide roles flipping depending on num_digits' sign -- a small new algorithm, not a 1-2-output composition, so this clears the bar for `candidate` rather than `composable-skip`/`composable-author`. Recommend a fixed small-arity signed cell (e.g. `excel_rounddown_i16(number: i16, num_digits: i16) -> i16`, tier matching `matrix_solve_3x3`'s precedent of "new capability, own cell" over decomposing into pieces spread across packs).

entries.name: ROUNDUP
entries.description: Rounds a number up, away from zero
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: Not a composition -- no clean 1-2-cell glue exists (see reason). A new cell would borrow (inline, since cells can't call each other) pow_checked_u32's checked-exponentiation technique for the 10^|num_digits| scale, div_ceil_u32's q+1-if-remainder ceiling technique, and the smag_* pack's (magnitude, sign) decomposition convention (e.g. smag_mul/smag_add's neg-field pattern) for both the signed number and the signed num_digits.
entries.repr: checked-int -- sibling to checked-arithmetic's existing rounding kernels (div_ceil_u32, round_div_checked_u32, pow_checked_u32), not f32 (softfloat pack has no ceiling/round primitive at all, only fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/lerp_f32/norm2_f32) and not a fixed-small-arity shape (matrix_solve_3x3's precedent is about multi-variable arity, irrelevant here -- ROUNDUP is naturally 2-argument already). New logic needed: sign-magnitude split of the number (mag, neg) and of num_digits (digits_mag, digits_neg); a checked 10^digits_mag scale (escalates past digits_mag ~9 in u32, matching pow_checked_u32's own overflow behavior); a branch on digits_neg choosing multiply-then-ceil-divide vs divide-then-ceil-multiply; and reattaching the number's original sign to the ceiling'd magnitude for the away-from-zero convention (distinct from a plain toward-positive-infinity ceiling).
entries.reason: No cell80 cell does decimal-place rounding at all, let alone the away-from-zero variant. checked-arithmetic has the pieces a caller might reach for -- div_ceil_u32 (id: div_ceil_u32, ceiling division), pow_checked_u32 (id: pow_checked_u32, checked base^exp for a 10^n scale factor), round_div_checked_u32 (round-to-nearest, wrong tie rule anyway) -- and fractions has frac_of_whole_ceil (id: frac_of_whole_ceil, ceil(n/d*whole)), the closest existing shape to "ceil(number*10^digits)". None of these compose at the call site into ROUNDUP(number, num_digits) because real Excel ROUNDUP has two independent sign branches that a 1-2-cell glue can't cover: (1) away-from-zero on the NUMBER's sign -- ceiling the magnitude then reattaching the original sign, not the plain positive-only ceiling div_ceil_u32/frac_of_whole_ceil perform; and (2) a sign branch on NUM_DIGITS itself -- digits>=0 means multiply-by-10^d-then-ceil-divide-back, digits<0 means DIVIDE-by-10^|d| then ceil-multiply-back, an inverted operation direction, not a parameter tweak. That two-axis case analysis is exactly the taxonomy amendment's reason-2 flag ("multi-step case analysis... usually isn't glue-composable at all, belongs in candidate") -- so per the amendment's own correction discipline (the NPV/IRR precedent) this is filed as candidate rather than composable-author.

entries.name: SIGN
entries.description: Returns the sign of a number
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: sign_i16
entries.repr: i16 (signed 16-bit), matches Excel's single-argument SIGN(number) exactly; no fixed-point or float variant needed since sign is representation-agnostic and the existing cell already covers the integer domain used elsewhere in the library (e.g. negate_i16, abs_i16 siblings in signed-deltas).
entries.reason: Excel's SIGN(number) returns 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if zero -- exactly the signed-deltas pack's `sign_i16` cell (docs/cell-index.md line 792): `run(x: i16) -> i16`, doc comment verbatim "Sign of a signed value: 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if zero." Same domain (i16 signed integer), same three-way output convention, no representation gap (Excel's SIGN operates on a single numeric argument, no array-state or arbitrary-arity issue like NPV/SUM had). This is a direct semantic and signature match, not a composition of other cells (negate_i16 and abs_i16 exist in the same pack but sign_i16 is already its own named cell, distinct per its own doc comment from both).

entries.name: SQRT
entries.description: Returns a positive square root
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: nth_root_f32 (docs/cell-index.md line 547), called with the exponent field n fixed to the literal constant 2 — x such that x^2 = c is exactly sqrt(c)
entries.reason: No cell80 cell is literally SQRT(x) at the f32 tier — `norm2_f32` only exposes sqrt(x*x+y*y) (2-arg vector norm, not bare sqrt), and softfloat.rs's fsqrt kernel is otherwise only ever inlined inside larger cells (excel_tbilleq's "one fsqrt", nth_root_f32's Newton seed), never wrapped standalone. But `nth_root_f32(c, n)` (numerical-primitives pack) already computes x such that x^n=c for a caller-supplied whole exponent n, and for n=2 that IS exactly sqrt(c) — its own docstring even says the Newton loop is "sqrt-seeded". So this is technically composable (one existing cell, n pinned to the literal 2, no new algorithm needed) and cite-able as such. It clears composable-author's reason 1 (well-known/expected): SQRT is as canonical a "well-known numerical method" as the taxonomy doc's own reason-1 examples (gcd, crc32) and Excel's own description ("returns a positive square root") maps almost verbatim onto nth_root_f32's domain restriction ("positive f32 value c"). This mirrors real precedent already in the library: bps_rate_over_2_periods (the fixed N=2 case of the sqrt-based rate recovery) was kept as its own cell even after excel_rri/nth_root_f32 generalized it to arbitrary N — the project's established practice is to author the well-known fixed-parameter specialization even when a general cell subsumes it, not fold it away or leave it uncovered.

entries.name: SQRTPI
entries.description: Returns the square root of (number * pi)
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: q_mul + q_sqrt (both in fixed-point pack, docs/cell-index.md lines ~343-344), fed number_q8 (via int_to_q8) and the Q8.8 pi literal 804 -- the same constant geom_circle_area_approx and geom_circle_circumference_approx already use (docs/cell-index.md lines 387-388)
entries.repr: Q8.8 fixed-point (fixed-point pack) -- caller-sequenced q_mul then q_sqrt
entries.reason: SQRTPI(number) = sqrt(number*pi) is a two-step composition of already-shipped Q8.8 fixed-point cells: q_mul(number_q8, PI_Q8) then q_sqrt(that product), reusing the exact Q8.8 pi constant (804 = round(3.14159265*256)) already established by geom_circle_area_approx/geom_circle_circumference_approx. Neither composable-author reason applies: reason 1 (well-known/expected) fails because there's no fragile sign/rounding/omitted-arg convention to encode -- it's one multiply by a known constant plus one sqrt, strictly simpler than the SLN row (`(cost-salvage)/life`) that the taxonomy doc already ruled composable-skip for the same reason. Reason 2 (genuine complexity) fails outright -- no iteration, no case analysis, just glue of two outputs. q_mul/q_sqrt's unsigned u16 domain also happens to match Excel's own restriction that SQRTPI's argument be non-negative (negative input is #NUM! in Excel), so there's no domain mismatch motivating a new cell either.

entries.name: TRUNC
entries.description: Truncates a number to an integer
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: div_i16(x, 256) — composes cell80/cells/signed-deltas/div_i16.rs (truncating signed division via sign-magnitude) with the fixed-point pack's Q8.8 scale constant 256 as the divisor
entries.composable_author_reason: well-known/expected functionality with convention fragility: TRUNC's toward-zero truncation is easily confused with floor/INT (they only diverge on negative inputs), the exact "rounding rule easy to get subtly wrong" class the taxonomy amendment names as earning a canonical cell even when technically glue.
entries.repr: Composition target is signed Q8.8 fixed-point (i16 domain), reusing div_i16 as-is with divisor=256; no new cell logic required for the num_digits=0 default case Excel's own one-liner describes.
entries.reason: Excel's TRUNC(number, [num_digits]) truncates toward zero (distinct from INT/floor, which rounds toward -infinity — they differ only on negative inputs: TRUNC(-8.9)=-8 vs INT(-8.9)=-9). num_digits is a scalar optional arg defaulting to 0, not an array — no array-state-field blocker here. For the default/common case Excel's own one-liner describes ("truncates a number to an integer"), cell80 already has a cell that does exactly this arithmetic: `div_i16` (cell80/cells/signed-deltas/div_i16.rs) computes signed i16 a/b via sign-magnitude (mag_a/mag_b, quotient truncated, sign = XOR of input signs) — i.e. genuine truncate-toward-zero division, verified straight from source. For a signed Q8.8-encoded number x, calling `div_i16(x, 256)` reproduces TRUNC(x/256) exactly: the caller just supplies the fixed-point pack's own scale constant (256) as div_i16's second argument, a one-cell, constant-arg composition. This is deliberately NOT what the pack's dedicated Q8.8 decode cell `q_to_int_i16` does — that one is documented as an arithmetic right shift that "floors toward negative infinity for negatives," i.e. it implements INT, not TRUNC, and the two cells coexist in the index specifically flagging this fault line. No cell id containing "trunc" exists in docs/cell-index.md (checked). Classifying composable-author rather than composable-skip because reason 1 (well-known/expected functionality) applies with real convention fragility: truncate-toward-zero vs. floor is exactly the "rounding rule that's easy to get subtly wrong re-deriving by hand each time" the taxonomy amendment names as justifying authorship even though it's glue — the same class of case as the amendment's own PMT/FV/PV example, and Excel itself keeps TRUNC and INT as two separate named functions for this reason. (The full num_digits!=0 decimal-place case would need additional power-of-10 scaling logic beyond this base composition, but that's outside what Excel's own quoted one-line description covers.)

entries.name: CORREL
entries.description: Returns the correlation coefficient between two data sets
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_correlation_sums_step (loop, one call per (x,y) pair) -> correlation (final call on accumulated sums)
entries.repr: Q8.8 fixed-point, bounded [-1,1] by construction (correlation's r_mag/r_neg output)
entries.reason: Excel's CORREL(array1, array2) is Pearson's r over two arbitrary-length arrays. cell80 already has the exact algebraic core landed as `correlation` (cell80/cells/statistics/correlation.rs — Pearson r = (n*sum_xy - sum_x*sum_y) / sqrt((n*sum_x2-sum_x^2)*(n*sum_y2-sum_y^2)), returned as Q8.8 bounded to [-1,1] by Cauchy-Schwarz), and the raw-array-to-sums aggregation step it explicitly defers upstream is already covered by `running_correlation_sums_step` (cell80/cells/running-stats/running_correlation_sums_step.rs), which folds one (x,y) pair per call into the six sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) that `correlation` consumes -- state threaded explicitly through scalar in/out struct fields each call (caller-sequenced, not relying on the broken host-persisted array-state mechanism). So CORREL is fully reproduced by the caller running `running_correlation_sums_step` once per paired element across both arrays, then a single call to `correlation` on the final sums -- exactly the 'raw-dataset aggregation stays upstream' convention this pack already documents identically for covariance/linear_regression_slope/linear_regression_intercept/sample_covariance_from_sums. Both pieces already exist and this composition pattern is the pack's established idiom, so neither composable-author reason applies (nothing new needs authoring, and the composition is plain glue, not a hidden algorithm) -- composable-skip.

entries.name: COVARIANCE.P
entries.description: Returns covariance, the average of the products of paired deviations
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_covariance_step (looped once per data pair, host-threads n/sum_x/sum_y/sum_xy forward as scalar in/out) -> covariance(n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy)
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is COVARIANCE.P(array1, array2) — an arbitrary-length paired-array reduction, so per the arity discipline (don't credit a fixed-arity sibling as "covered" for an arbitrary-arity real signature) no single existing cell covers it directly.
