But it composes cleanly, with no new logic: the statistics pack already ships a purpose-built streaming accumulator (`running_covariance_step`, running-stats pack) whose own docstring says it exists specifically to feed `covariance` (statistics pack) — the host loops it once per (x,y) pair, threading the scalar sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy) forward call-to-call (ordinary sequential composition, not an array-typed argument, so the array-state-field gap that sinks NPV doesn't apply here), then calls `covariance` once on the final sums: cov = (n*sum_xy - sum_x*sum_y)/n^2, which is exactly the COVARIANCE.P population formula, returned as an exact signed fraction. Neither composable-author reason clears the bar: reason 2 (genuine complexity) fails because the final step is one arithmetic expression, no iteration/convergence. Reason 1 (well-known/expected, convention fragility) is the closer call -- population-vs-sample divisor confusion (n vs n-1) is a classic fragile stats convention -- but that fragility is already resolved by the library's existing split naming (`covariance` = population ÷n², `sample_covariance_from_sums` = sample ÷n(n-1), for COVARIANCE.S), so a new COVARIANCE.P wrapper cell would add no new disambiguation, just a redundant compatibility-named shim. This matches the taxonomy amendment's SLN precedent (glue, not algorithm; no *unresolved* fragile convention) rather than the PMT precedent.

entries.name: COVARIANCE.S
entries.description: Returns the sample covariance
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: sample_covariance_from_sums
entries.repr: u16-packed exact signed fraction (num_mag/den, num_neg sign bit) over checked-int sums; formula cov = (n*sum_xy - sum_x*sum_y) / (n*(n-1))
entries.reason: Excel's COVARIANCE.S(array1, array2) = Σ(x-x̄)(y-ȳ)/(n-1), the unbiased (Bessel-corrected) sample covariance from an arbitrary-length array pair. cell80's `sample_covariance_from_sums` (docs/cell-index.md:847, cell80/cells/statistics/sample_covariance_from_sums.rs) computes cov = (n*sum_xy - sum_x*sum_y) / (n*(n-1)) from precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy) -- the standard raw-sums identity, algebraically identical to Excel's centered-moment formula, returned as an exact fraction rather than rounded. This is not the array-state-field gap that sank NPV: NPV needed each array element independently (discounted at a distinct power of the rate), so it couldn't be reduced to a few scalars. Covariance/variance/correlation are 'sufficient-statistics' computations -- the whole array collapses losslessly into four running sums, which `running_covariance_step` (cell-index.md:692) already exists to accumulate one (x,y) pair at a time across a stream (scalar state only, no array round-trip). This is the exact same precomputed-sums framing docs/math-server-map.md already established and used to land the population-covariance sibling `covariance` (cell-index.md:843) and `correlation` (cell-index.md:842) -- COVARIANCE.S is the Bessel's-correction sibling of that same population `covariance` cell, and cell80 already ships that sibling by name (`sample_covariance_from_sums`, explicitly documented as the Bessel's-correction counterpart to `covariance`'s population framing). Host workflow: stream pairs through running_covariance_step to build (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy), then call sample_covariance_from_sums once -- same two-call pattern already used for covariance/correlation, not a new gap.

entries.name: PEARSON
entries.description: Returns the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_correlation_sums_step (cell80/cells/running-stats/running_correlation_sums_step.rs) run by the host once per (x,y) pair across array1/array2, folding forward its (count, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) state, then those six final sums fed as inputs to correlation (cell80/cells/statistics/correlation.rs) for the Q8.8 Pearson r
entries.reason: Excel's PEARSON(array1, array2) has two parts: (a) aggregate six raw sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) over an arbitrary-length pair of arrays, and (b) compute r = (n*sum_xy - sum_x*sum_y) / sqrt((n*sum_x2-sum_x^2)*(n*sum_y2-sum_y^2)) from those sums. Both already exist in cell80 and were purpose-built for exactly this pairing: `running_correlation_sums_step` (cell80/cells/running-stats/running_correlation_sums_step.rs, cell-index.md line 691) streams the aggregation one (x,y) pair at a time via scalar state fields (count, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) that the host round-trips call-to-call -- its own doc comment names 'statistics/correlation' as the consumer it was built for. `correlation` (cell80/cells/statistics/correlation.rs, cell-index.md line 842) takes those six precomputed sums and returns Pearson's r as a Q8.8 fixed-point value bounded to [-1,1] by construction. This is not the array-state-field gap (a single cell trying to hold a variable-length array in one struct, which the runner genuinely can't do -- that's what makes NPV host_only) -- it's the accepted 'caller runs a running_*_step cell in sequence across the array, then feeds the final state into a formula cell' composition, the same pattern covariance/linear_regression_slope/intercept already rely on. Since the fragile part of the formula (signed numerator, product-then-sqrt-then-divide ordering, Cauchy-Schwarz bound) is already captured by the existing `correlation` cell, there's no gap left to justify authoring a new cell under either composable-author reason -- composable-skip.

entries.name: RSQ
entries.description: Returns the square of the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_correlation_sums_step (called once per (known_x_i, known_y_i) pair, caller running it in sequence to build n/sum_x/sum_y/sum_xy/sum_x2/sum_y2 -- cell-index.md line 691) -> correlation (Pearson r as Q8.8 in [-1,1], line 842) -> q_mul(r, r) (Q8.8 fixed-point multiply, fixed-point pack, line 338) to get r^2 = RSQ. No new cell needed; three existing cells, the last a trivial self-multiply.
entries.reason: RSQ(known_y's, known_x's) = r^2, the Pearson correlation coefficient squared. Excel's real signature is arbitrary-length paired arrays, same shape as CORREL -- but unlike NPV's cash-flow list (ruled host_only in docs/excel-financial-map.md because no existing cell reduces it), cell80's statistics pack already solves the arbitrary-length-aggregation problem for exactly this computation via a streaming accumulator: running_correlation_sums_step (cell-index.md:691) takes one (x,y) pair plus the running six sums per call and is designed for the caller to run it in sequence over the whole dataset ("nothing downstream needs a raw-dataset re-pass"), then `correlation` (line 842) finalizes those sums into r as a Q8.8 value in [-1,1] by construction. entries.name: SLOPE
entries.description: Returns the slope of the linear regression line
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: linear_regression_slope
entries.repr: LinearRegressionSlope::run() -> u16
entries.reason: Excel's SLOPE(known_y's, known_x's) = (n*Σxy - Σx*Σy) / (n*Σx² - (Σx)²), the ordinary-least-squares slope. cell80's linear_regression_slope (docs/cell-index.md:846) computes exactly this formula from precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2), returned as an exact signed fraction. Raw-dataset aggregation over the arrays stays upstream (host-side loop, or streamed via running_correlation_sums_step, docs/cell-index.md:691) -- this is a position-independent running sum (order of pairs doesn't matter), unlike NPV's per-element discount-exponent dependency that forced NPV to host_only in docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's correction. docs/math-server-map.md confirms linear_regression_slope was landed in Wave 13 specifically as an exact-name match alongside covariance (matching the CORREL/COVARIANCE.P family), establishing this precomputed-sums pattern as the accepted 'covered' shape for this whole statistics pack rather than a composable-author gap.

entries.name: INTERCEPT
entries.description: Returns the intercept of the linear regression line
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: linear_regression_intercept
entries.repr: Exact signed fraction (num_mag, num_neg over den), sharing linear_regression_slope's denominator (n^2 times the population variance of x) -- not rounded to a float/fixed-point value.
entries.reason: docs/cell-index.md:845 has `linear_regression_intercept` (`LinearRegressionIntercept::run() -> u16`): "Ordinary-least-squares regression intercept from precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2 -- the same five sums linear_regression_slope consumes): b = (sum_y*sum_x2 - sum_x*sum_xy) / (n*sum_x2 - sum_x^2)". That closed form is exactly Excel INTERCEPT's definition (the constant term of the OLS fit line, same denominator n*sum_x2 - sum_x^2 that its sibling `linear_regression_slope` (line 846) uses). The five input sums are themselves produced by streaming one (x,y) pair per call through `running_correlation_sums_step` (line 691) -- a fold/accumulator pattern (state threaded call-to-call as scalars), not the arbitrary-arity array-state-field gap that sank NPV, since the host just loops feeding one pair at a time rather than needing Excel's whole known_y's/known_x's array in a single call. So both halves of Excel's real pipeline (aggregate the arrays, then compute the intercept) are already covered by existing cells; the intercept computation itself is a direct, exact match, not an approximation or a narrower-arity stand-in.

entries.name: STEYX
entries.description: Returns the standard error of the predicted y-value for each x in the regression
entries.repr: statistics-from-sums tier, matching correlation/std_dev_from_sums precedent (cell-index.md lines 842, 849): consume the 6 raw precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) via checked u32 arithmetic, form SSE = Syy - Sxy^2/Sxx (or the Syy*(1-r^2) / Syy-slope*Sxy identity), divide by the new (n-2) regression-residual-degrees-of-freedom denominator, then take the same branch-free bitwise integer square root correlation.rs/std_dev_from_sums.rs already inline -- new logic: the Sxy^2/Sxx cross term combine (or reuse of correlation's r^2 / linear_regression_slope's fraction) plus the (n-2) denominator convention, neither of which any existing cell currently derives.
entries.reason: No existing cell computes this (grepped cell-index.md for residual/std_error/steyx/sse/forecast/trend — nothing). Excel's real signature STEYX(known_y's, known_x's) takes two arbitrary-length arrays, but the statistics pack's established convention (correlation, covariance, linear_regression_slope/intercept, variance_from_sums, sample_variance_from_sums, std_dev_from_sums, sample_covariance_from_sums — all at cell-index.md lines 842-850) already sidesteps that array-state-field gap by taking precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2) as fixed-arity input, raw-dataset aggregation left upstream. STEYX fits that same precomputed-sums design, so it is not host_only for the array reason (unlike NPV's genuine arbitrary-valued-list gap, per the taxonomy doc's correction note). But no cell exposes the needed intermediate: STEYX = sqrt(SSE/(n-2)) where SSE = Syy - Sxy^2/Sxx (Syy=(n*sum_y2-sum_y^2)/n, Sxy=(n*sum_xy-sum_x*sum_y)/n, Sxx=(n*sum_x2-sum_x^2)/n; equivalently SSE = Syy*(1-r^2) using correlation's r, or Syy - slope*Sxy using linear_regression_slope's output). Every route requires re-deriving Sxy/Syy/Sxx afresh (not exposed by any existing cell's output) plus a brand-new degrees-of-freedom denominator convention (n-2, distinct from every existing from-sums cell's n or n*(n-1)) plus a final sqrt -- more than gluing 1-2 existing outputs, and it matches how correlation/std_dev_from_sums/linear_regression_slope were each authored as their own single from-sums cell rather than composed from each other. So this is a new from-sums statistics cell, not composable-skip or composable-author.

entries.name: STANDARDIZE
entries.description: Returns a normalized value (z-score)
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: zscore_q8 (cell80/cells/running-stats/zscore_q8.rs)
entries.repr: Q8.8 fixed-point (i16)
entries.reason: Excel's STANDARDIZE(x, mean, standard_dev) = (x - mean) / standard_dev is a fixed 3-argument function, not an array-state case. cell80's existing zscore_q8 (`run(value_q8: i16, mean_q8: i16, stddev_q8: i16) -> i16`, docs/cell-index.md line 703) computes exactly this: `(diff << 8) / stddev_q8` where `diff = value_q8 - mean_q8`, in Q8.8 fixed-point, with the same safe_div-style zero-guard convention (returns 0 if stddev_q8 <= 0) that the rest of the library uses instead of panicking/erroring. The cell's own doc-comment tag line even lists "standardize" as an explicit alias tag, so this was already recognized as the STANDARDIZE-equivalent when authored. No new logic or composition needed — this is a direct hit, not composable-skip/author.

entries.name: DEVSQ
entries.description: Returns the sum of squares of deviations
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_variance_step (running-stats pack) — stream raw values one per call, read its `m2` state field directly (skip the div_floor_u32(m2,count) step that would turn it into VARP). Equivalent alternate route from precomputed sums: variance_from_sums's `num` field (statistics pack) combined with the caller-known `n` gives DEVSQ = num/n exactly.
entries.reason: Excel's real signature is DEVSQ(number1, [number2], ...) — arbitrary-arity raw data, sum((x_i - mean)^2). Unlike NPV (host_only precedent), this exact function family (VAR/VARP/STDEV/STDEVP/DEVSQ) already has an established cell80 answer to the arity problem: stream one raw value per call through running_variance_step (running-stats pack), carrying (count, sum, m2) as host-managed scalar state between calls — the same idiom running_correlation_sums_step/running_covariance_step use elsewhere. running_variance_step's own docstring says "Compose with div_floor_u32(m2, count) for the variance itself" — meaning m2, BEFORE that division, is already the raw sum of squared deviations from the mean, i.e. exactly DEVSQ, with zero further arithmetic. Alternatively, if the caller already holds precomputed sums (n, sum_x, sum_x2), variance_from_sums's `num` field (= n*sum_x2 - sum_x^2, statistics pack) paired with the already-known n gives DEVSQ = num/n as an exact fraction, again no new cell. Neither composable-author reason applies: no fragile sign/rounding/default-argument convention (reason 1 — matches the SLN precedent, which resolved composable-skip for the same reason), and no iteration/convergence/multi-case algorithm (reason 2) — running_variance_step already does all the algorithmic work; DEVSQ is just "read m2, don't divide."

entries.name: GEOMEAN
entries.description: Returns the geometric mean
entries.missing_capability: Arbitrary-arity argument aggregation across a call boundary. Excel's real signature is GEOMEAN(number1, [number2], ..., [number255]) — an unbounded list of independently-valued numbers reduced (product, then Nth root) in a single call. CellHost's runner only round-trips named SCALAR fields per run() and zeros state each run() (confirmed, docs/cell-index.md / experiments/sliding-window-state-cells-findings.md); there is no array/buffer field a fixed cell struct could hold N values in, and a fixed struct can't represent unbounded N anyway. This is the identical gap NPV was corrected to host_only for in docs/excel-financial-map.md / cell80/data/excel_financial_catalog_map.json ("array-state fields ... CellHost's runner only round-trips named scalar fields ... cannot be passed in") — same missing capability, different function.
entries.reason: cell80 has geomean2 (docs/cell-index.md line 712: "Integer geometric mean of two u16 values, floor(sqrt(a*b))") — but that is a FIXED 2-arity sibling, not GEOMEAN's real arbitrary-arity signature, exactly the mistake the taxonomy doc's NPV correction warns against ("a FIXED small-arity sibling existing does NOT make an arbitrary-arity Excel function covered — classify against Excel's REAL signature"). Excel's GEOMEAN takes 1-255 arguments and returns (x1*x2*...*xn)^(1/n). Note the arithmetic itself is not the blocker: nth_root_f32 already exists ("General Nth root of a positive f32 value c ... via a sqrt-seeded, bounded Newton-Raphson refinement", docs/cell-index.md line 547) so a general fractional-exponent root is available in the f32 tier, and a running product could in principle be accumulated the way running_variance_step/running_mad_step thread scalar accumulator state call-to-call. What's missing is the ability to feed Excel's actual single-call, arbitrary-N argument list into any cell at all — the same array-state-field gap that forced NPV's correction from composable-author to host_only in Wave 1 (docs/coverage-map-taxonomy-amendment.md's Part 4 correction note, and cell80/data/excel_financial_catalog_map.json's NPV row). A fixed small-arity sibling (geomean3/geomean4, following ranking-stats' median3/4/mode3/4 precedent — product via mul_u16_u16_to_u32-style checked widening, then nth_root_f32 with n hardcoded to 3 or 4) would be legitimate future candidate work, but graded against GEOMEAN's actual Excel signature this is host_only today, not composable-author and not candidate.
